instruction: I need better visual contrast on my screen. Can you enable a high contrast theme to make elements more distinguishable?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: THEME=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme 2>/dev/null | tr -d "'"); if echo "$THEME" | grep -iq 'contrast'; then echo "High contrast theme enabled: $THEME"; else echo "No high contrast theme"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling a high contrast theme for better visual distinction. The evaluator checks if the gtk-theme setting contains 'contrast' (case-insensitive), which indicates a high contrast theme is active. Common high contrast themes in Ubuntu include 'HighContrast', 'HighContrastInverse', etc. This is verified by checking gsettings for org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme.
metadata.verification: Verified that gsettings command checks for gtk-theme containing 'contrast' keyword, which is standard for high contrast themes in GNOME/Ubuntu
